cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Acknowledge Our History
cards.instruction: Make someone recognize that the relationship, memory, or sacrifice mattered and cannot be treated as incidental.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Before you box our allotment photo, admit that summer wasn't wasted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We grew three carrots. I need the shelf.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. You got out of bed every morning to water those three carrots with me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I could put the photo on my desk at work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Would you? And tell people that part when they laugh at the harvest.

mechanism: A authorizes where a shared photograph may go only if its emotional significance receives explicit credit.
confusable: D77 shares current burden; D81 insists a past relationship or memory not be dismissed as incidental.
comparison: A small harvest photo becoming a public desk memory differs from preserving a receipt for a missed-ferry weekend.
seedUse: Use D81-a helpful desk offer as the next vehicle for acknowledgment; do not copy it into unrelated pairs.
